summary: Station established 1832 at the entrance to Port Clyde Harbor, Maine; the granite tower dates from 1857, and the grounds and museum are open to visitors.

lens.note: USLHS: original fifth-order Fresnel, installed 1857. Current optic: VLB-44 LED, installed 2016 (USLHS).

fog_signal.note: Bell struck by machinery, established 10 August 1898 (LHB 1899).

structures.note: Round granite tower, 24 ft (7.3 m) from base to focal plane of the original lens (NRHP). Replaced the first tower, whose shape and location are unknown (NRHP).
Old stone dwelling demolished and a new wooden dwelling built on its foundation (LHB 1896). USLHS gives 1895; NRHP gives 1896.
NRHP gives 1905 for the granite oil house; USLHS gives 1898.

access.note: Grounds open year-round, dawn to dusk; the museum is closed for the 2026 season; the site is free to visit (owner's site).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS gives keepers' quarters 1895 and NRHP gives 1896. The 1895 Board report records lightning damage in June 1895 and a contract to rebuild; the 1896 report records the old stone house demolished and a new wooden dwelling built. Read together, the contract was 1895 and the work was done in 1896.

notes_for_editor: 1) Station record structure 'tower, brick, built 1832' disagrees with NRHP and USLHS (granite, 1857): proposed correction. 2) Keeper's dwelling: USLHS 1895, NRHP 1896; resolved as contract 1895, built 1896 (resolved_conflicts). 3) Oil house: NRHP 1905 vs USLHS 1898; not used in the story, unresolved. 4) First lighting: station record gives 1832 and 1858; USLHS gives the lens in 1857. The story gives only 'established 1832' and the tower of 1857. 5) Pierce's 1921 transfer: the Kennebec Journal OCR reads '1S91' for the year he entered the ranks; read as 1891, check the page image. 6) The Kennebec Journal (1921) also reports Pierce's rescue of the crew of a British schooner in a six-hour battle with weather; the place is not given, so it is not in the story. 7) Bulletin 1929 p.34 (PDF): the keeper's name is spaced in the OCR ('E . H. Pierce'), and the yacht's name is garbled; check the page image. 8) Bulletin 1927 p.45 has a fire near the station (tender Tulip assisting); the index attributes the fire to a keeper 'E.L. Pierce'. Not used: the OCR is garbled. 9) Lifesaving Service tables list 'Marshalls Point' among stations and wrecks (1898, 1901, 1902, 1903); these are OCR'd tables with no legible wreck narrative for this point; not used. 10) Roster lines matched by name and position (0.09 km). 11) Station record characteristic ('F W') and range (13 nm) are not verified here; omitted. 12) Visiting information comes from the owner's site on 2026-10-22; the museum's season is as the site states it. 13) The 1832 keeper John Watts and the early roster are the USLHS list, not checked against NARA registers. 14) Fact-check 2026-10-22: footnote 10 is the owner's home page, the only page read for the 2026 season, dawn-to-dusk hours, free admission and fundraiser; no inner page was available. The 1921 Kennebec Journal year of entry is OCR 'in 1S91', read as 1891 (story footnote says so): check the page image before print. The 1929 Bulletin item was matched by PDF page 34; its yacht name is garbled and not used.
